text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

WHEAT SALE - South Korea's Cheiljedang Corp and Dongah Flour Mills Co Ltd jointly bought 21,000 tonnes of U.S. No.1 wheat from Japanese trading house Mitsubishi Corp, company officials said. Shipment was set for June 5-July 5 to the western port of Inchon.
USDA said Wednesday private exporters reported sales of 110,000 tonnes of hard red winter wheat to unknown destinations for delivery during the 1997/98 marketing year.

SOYBEAN SALE - Grains traders in Hong Kong and China confirmed on Wednesday that China last week bought at least two lots of U.S. soybeans, more expensive than South American beans, for delivery in June, sold at under $350 per tonne C&F.
SOYOIL SALES - State-owned Taiwan Sugar Corp bought a shipment of 2,500 tonnes of South American soyoil at a tender on Wednesday, company officials said.
- A commercial firm bought 7,000 tonnes of Brazilian soyoil Wednesday for shipment to China for May delivery, U.S. exporters said.

BARLEY SALE - Turkey's state grain board said Wednesday it awarded its 100,000-tonne feed barley tender equally to Glencore at $142.29 per tonne and to Alfred Toepfer at $142.12 per tonne with both shipments in May, grain officials said.

WHEAT TENDERS - South Korea's Cheiljedang Corp and Dongah Flour Mills Co Ltd have jointly invited tenders to buy a total of 23,500 tonnes of U.S. No.1 wheat by 2:00 p.m. (0500 GMT) on Friday. Shipment was set for June 5-July5 to Inchon.
- South Korea's Daehan Flour Mills Co Ltd has invited tenders to buy 22,000 tonnes of U.S. No.1 wheat on Friday, traders said. Shipment was set for June 20-July 20 to Inchon.

WHEAT TENDERS - Sri Lanka's Co-operative Wholesale Establishment seeks 100,000 tonnes of hard wheat in 50,000-tonne lots, government officials said. Tenders close on May 16 with the first shipment for May 22-June 5 if from the U.S., Canada, Europe or Argentina, and June 10-19 from Australia or Saudi Arabia. The second shipment was for June 16-25 if from U.S., Canada, the Continent or Argentina, and June 30-July 9 from Australia or Saudi Arabia.
- South Korea's Cheiljedang Corp and Dongah Flour Mills Co Ltd have jointly invited tenders to buy a total of 23,500 tonnes of U.S. No.1 wheat on Friday for June 1-30 shipment.

WHEAT TENDERS - - Pakistan will issue a tender on Saturday for 315,000 tonnes of soft white wheat from the United States or Australia for shipment between May 20 and June 10, an official at the Agriculture Ministry said.
CORN TENDER - The CCC was to seek on May 1 for up to 50,000 tonnes of U.S. corn for donation to North Korea. The corn is for May 10-June 10 shipment.
SOYBEAN TENDER - CCC was to tender April 30 for up to 10,000 tonnes of U.S. yellow soybeans for export to Ukraine, for May 10-June 5 shipment.
SUNOIL TENDER - The CCC was tendering on May 7 for 3,000 tonnes of U.S. crude sunflower seed oil for export to Mozambique, June 1-20 shipment.

RICE TENDERS - Costa Rica postponed for a second time a rice tender for 26,500 tonnes of rough rice or 18,000 tonnes of dehusked rice because of high international prices, a spokesman for the national rice industry said.
- Jordan seeks to buy 15,000 tonnes of medium grain camolina type rice for delivery in June, traders said. The closing date for offers is May 21.

COMMODITY TENDERS - South Korea's National Livestock Cooperatives Federation seeks to buy 50,000 tonnes of tapioca hard pellet on Friday for June-September arrival. It also invites tenders to buy 30,000 tonnes of wheat bran pellet or rice bran pellet on the same day for July 10 and September 10 arrival. If NLCF passes in whole or part due to high prices, it will re-invite the tenders on May 6.

- The CCC will tender April 29 for pinto beans, sunflower oil, bulgur and wheat-soy blend for donation to Moldova. It seeks 255 tonnes of pinto beans, 605 tonnes of sunflower oil, 510 tonnes of bulgur (cracked wheat), and 255 tonnes of a wheat-soy blend. The beans, bulgur and wheat-soy blend were for June 6-20 shipment and the oil was for June 20-July 5.

MARKET TALK - Egypt's expected wheat harvest of 5.9 million tonnes and its flush reserves will keep it out of the grain market until at least December, the main official in charge of government commodity purchases said on Wednesday.

- The Thai feed and livestock industry made further purchases of soymeal and soybeans over the week, traders said. One Thai crusher bought 50,000 tonnes of Brazilian soybeans for June delivery and a vessel was now loading the consignment at a Brazilian port.
